title: B002: Implement Kubernetes-interacting packages
summary: Implements 7 Kubernetes-client-dependent packages within internal/common/: config/ extension (CreateImmutableConfigMap), secrets/ (IsExternalSecretReady, IsSecretReady, GetSecretValue, EnsurePushSecret), database/ (EnsureDatabase, EnsureDatabaseUser, RunDBSyncJob), deployment/ (EnsureDeployment, EnsureService, IsDeploymentReady), job/ (RunJob, EnsureCronJob, IsJobComplete), tls/ (EnsureCertificate, GetTLSSecret), and policy/ extension (LoadPolicyFromConfigMap). Adds SimulateCertificateReady and SimulatePushSecretReady to testutil/simulators/. All packages have envtest integration tests, doc.go files, and comprehensive reference documentation. All unit tests, integration tests, go vet, and golangci-lint pass cleanly.

architecture_findings.description: deployment/ and job/ packages use Get+Create/Update instead of server-side apply with field manager as specified in task 3.4. The spec called for 'client.Apply with ForceOwnership and FieldManager cobaltcore-operator'. The implemented approach uses optimistic concurrency via ResourceVersion, which is functionally correct and arguably more pragmatic for operator-owned resources. Function signatures also differ: spec called for variadic ownerRefs, implementation accepts pre-constructed objects with ownerRefs already set. This is a cleaner API for typed resources where callers construct the full object.
architecture_findings.fix: If SSA is later needed for multi-controller conflict resolution, refactor to use client.Apply with FieldManager. Current approach is fine for single-owner resources.

architecture_findings.description: database/RunDBSyncJob signature differs from spec: uses plain image string instead of types.ImageSpec, and accepts volumeMounts/volumes instead of env vars. These are practical improvements — volumeMounts are needed for config injection, and plain string avoids coupling to types.ImageSpec.
architecture_findings.fix: No action needed. If types.ImageSpec is later required for tag/digest resolution, refactor the signature.

architecture_findings.description: EnsureCertificate signature differs from spec: hardcodes issuerRef.kind to ClusterIssuer, derives secretName as name+'-tls', adds commonName parameter. These simplifications are appropriate given the current single-issuer use case.
architecture_findings.fix: If Issuer (namespace-scoped) support is needed later, add issuerKind/issuerGroup parameters.

The database/EnsureDatabaseUser always grants ALL privileges on *.* — document this as a known simplification if per-service privilege scoping is needed later

detected_patterns.name: Unstructured client for third-party CRDs, typed client for core resources
detected_patterns.applies_when: Creating or reading Kubernetes resources where no typed Go client exists (MariaDB, ESO, cert-manager CRDs)
detected_patterns.description: Third-party CRDs (MariaDB Database/User/Grant, ExternalSecret, PushSecret, Certificate) are managed via unstructured.Unstructured objects with explicit GVK, SetNestedField, and NestedSlice operations. Core K8s resources (ConfigMap, Secret, Deployment, Service, Job, CronJob) use typed clients from k8s.io/api. This avoids importing typed client libraries for operators that are not under our control.

detected_patterns.name: Idempotent create with AlreadyExists swallow
detected_patterns.applies_when: Creating Kubernetes resources that should be created once and not updated (unstructured CRDs, immutable ConfigMaps, Jobs)
detected_patterns.description: For resources that are created once and not updated (CRDs managed by external operators, immutable ConfigMaps, Jobs), the pattern is: attempt Create, if apierrors.IsAlreadyExists(err) return nil. For ConfigMap, a preliminary Get check is used since the content-hash name makes it a lookup. For resources that need updates (Deployment, Service, CronJob), the pattern is Get+Create/Update with ResourceVersion preservation.

detected_patterns.name: Integration test structure with TestMain and envtest
detected_patterns.applies_when: Writing integration tests for any package that interacts with the Kubernetes API
detected_patterns.description: Each package's integration test file follows: //go:build integration tag, package_test package, var k8sClient client.Client, const testNamespace, TestMain that calls testenvtest.SetupEnvTest(), creates a dedicated namespace, runs tests, and calls teardown. Individual tests use unique resource names and t.Cleanup for resource deletion. Unit tests for pure functions use //go:build !integration tag.

detected_patterns.name: Simulator pattern for envtest CRD controllers
detected_patterns.applies_when: Adding a new simulator for a third-party CRD operator (e.g. cert-manager, ESO, MariaDB)
detected_patterns.description: Each simulator is a single function in its own file that calls the shared simulateUnstructuredReady helper with the appropriate GVK, condition reason, and message. The helper uses createOrGet for idempotency, then patches status via client.MergeFrom with status.ready=true and a Ready condition. For CRDs needing custom status (like ExternalSecret which creates a target Secret), a dedicated implementation is used instead of the shared helper.

detected_patterns.name: Error wrapping with operation context
detected_patterns.applies_when: Returning errors from K8s API calls or field manipulation
detected_patterns.description: All errors are wrapped with fmt.Errorf using %w and include: the operation being performed, the resource namespace/name, and the original error. Pattern: fmt.Errorf("<verb>ing <Resource> %s/%s: %w", namespace, name, err). For unstructured field operations: fmt.Errorf("setting <Resource> <field.path>: %w", err).

examples.code: return false, fmt.Errorf("getting ExternalSecret %s/%s: %w", namespace, name, err)

detected_patterns.name: Content-hash naming for immutable resources
detected_patterns.applies_when: Creating ConfigMaps whose content must trigger rolling restarts when changed
detected_patterns.description: ConfigMaps are named {base}-{hash[:8]} where hash is SHA-256 of sorted key=value pairs. This ensures: (1) identical content produces identical names (idempotent), (2) different content produces different names (triggers rolling restart via pod template annotation), (3) old ConfigMaps are preserved until garbage-collected via owner references.
